(a) Any person having a complaint against any member of the governing authority for an alleged ethics violation shall file in writing a verified complaint setting forth the particular facts and circumstances which constitute the alleged violation. The complaint shall be filed with the city manager or city attorney. Upon receipt of a complaint the city manager or city attorney shall randomly draw the names of three members from the board of ethics pool. The three members along with the city attorney as legal counsel, shall constitute an investigating committee to determine whether the complaint sets forth significant facts and circumstances so as to warrant a hearing before the board of ethics. The investigating committee shall have the right to request supporting documentation from the complaining party if the committee deems it reasonable to avoid the pursuit of frivolous complaints. If the complaint does not set forth sufficient facts to constitute an alleged violation and is found unjustified, frivolous or patently unfounded, it shall be dismissed and the complainant notified immediately. If the complaint is found to state sufficient facts to warrant a hearing before the board of ethics, the board shall be appointed as provided in subsection (b).
(b) The board of ethics of the city shall be composed of seven registered voters of the city to be appointed as provided in this subsection. Each member of the board of ethics shall have been a resident of the city for at least one year immediately preceding the date of taking office and shall remain a resident of the city while serving as a member of the board of ethics. No person shall serve as a member of the board of ethics if the person has, or has had within the preceding one-year period, any interest in any contract, transaction or official action of the city. The mayor and council shall each appoint three qualified registered voters of the city to provide a pool of 18 individuals who have consented to serve as a member of such board of ethics and who will be available for a period of the term of their appointer to be called upon to serve in the event a board of ethics is appointed.
The city attorney shall maintain a listing of these 18 qualified registered voters of the city. Should the investigating committee determine a complaint warrants a hearing before the board of ethics, the mayor and council, at the first public meeting after such determination, shall draw names randomly from the listing of qualified citizens until the specified seven members of the board of ethics have been appointed. Such board will elect one of its members to serve as chairman.
The governing authority of the city shall provide a meeting space for the board of ethics. Subject to budgetary procedures and requirements of the city, the city shall provide the board of ethics with such supplies and equipment as may be reasonably necessary for it to perform its duties and responsibilities.
(c) Duties and powers. The constituted board of ethics shall have the following duties and powers:
(1) Establish procedures, rules and regulations governing its internal organization and conduct of its affairs.
(2) Hold a hearing within 60 days after the receipt of complaint.
(3) Prescribe forms, approved by the city attorney, for the disclosure required in this section and to make available to the public information disclosed as provided in this section.

(f) At the public hearing, the commission may grant, or deny for cause, the renewal of any license issued hereunder.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-29; Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
174:
(a) Summary action.
(1) If at any time during the holding of a license granted under this chapter, it should appear that the licensee has violated the provisions of this chapter, or the laws of the state or any federal laws, or if it should appear that the application contained known false information, or if it appears necessary for the public safety, health and welfare, the police chief of the city, his assistants who are acting under his authority, or any officially designated license inspector may request the commission to suspend or revoke the license to sell or consume any alcoholic beverages within the city.
(2) Reserved.
(3) The commission shall hold a hearing on such request for a revocation or suspension and after such hearing, the commission may revoke or suspend said license or place said licensee on probation.
(b) Action by the commission. The commission shall have full power and authority to revoke, refuse to renew, suspend or place on probation any licensee to sell or consume alcoholic beverages for violation of this chapter, or of the state or federal laws, or when said commission shall determine, after five days' notice and hearing that the operation of the licensed business is detrimental to the health, safety or welfare of the public. For the purpose of this section it shall be sufficient if notice is mailed, giving the time and place of the hearing by United States Certified Mail at the address of the licensee as shown in the application.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-30; Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
175:
In addition to the annual license fees required, there is hereby levied and imposed an excise tax which shall be paid to the city, as provided by Georgia Laws, on all malt beverages sold by each wholesale dealer within the area of the city.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-31)
176:
Tax shall be paid to the city by each wholesale dealer on all malt beverages sold within the city not later than the 10th day of each month, based upon the units of beverage sold during the previous calendar month by said wholesalers to retailers in the city.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-32)
177:
The wholesale dealer shall keep true and correct records of all sales and shipments and shall render a sworn statement of the name accompanying the monthly report to the city clerk, and said report shall show the exact quantities of malt beverages, by size and type of container and the amount of excise tax collected.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-33)
178:
The city shall have the right to audit, and to require production of records from each wholesaler supplying retailers in the area of the city, and also from each retailer so supplied.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-34)
179:
The failure to make a timely report and remittance of aforesaid taxes shall render a wholesale dealer liable for a penalty equal to ten percent of the total amount due, in addition to the amount due; and additionally if said report is not filed or if said taxes are not remitted and paid within 30 days from the date that the same are due, the city shall have the right to suspend and/or revoke any wholesale license, and further to prohibit said wholesaler from making any deliveries of any type whatsoever within the area of the city.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-35)
180:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell at retail or otherwise dispense beverages within the city on which the tax required in this article has not been paid to the wholesaler or distributor or to the city.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-36)
183:
(a) Unless the context demands otherwise, the words and terms used in this article shall have the same definition and meaning as state law where used in O.C.G.A. tit. 5A (Alcoholic Beverage).
(b) "Business location" shall mean the location or proposed location of a retail wine outlet.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-51)
184:
(a) A separate license shall be required for each wine outlet, and a separate application shall be made for each outlet.
(b) No license shall be transferable or assignable.
(c) Immediately upon the sale or closing of an outlet, it shall be the duty of the licensee to surrender the license to the city.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-52)
185:
License under this article shall be classified as follows:
(1) Retail which shall permit only the sale of wine in packages at retail.
(2) Wholesale-wholesale wine distributor, which shall permit only the sale of wine at wholesale.
The amount of the license fee for each class shall be set as set forth in the license schedule in section 6-62.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-53)
186:
Application for a retail package wine license shall be the same as, and in accordance with the requirements applicable to the sale of malt beverages by the package at retail, and all provisions in this chapter pertaining to the application and qualifications for a malt beverage license, including sections 6-3 through 6-9 shall be enforced in the sale of wine. All regulations controlling the sale of malt beverages shall also be applicable to the sale of wine as if fully set out as a separate section hereunder.
(Note: Wholesalers delivering wine on prior orders are not required to have a wine license when business is not located in city). It is the intention of this article that wine be sold either in conjunction with a qualified and licensed retail malt beverage outlet under the sale standards and restrictions as are applicable to retail malt beverage outlets, or if the licensee so desires that wine may be sold at a qualified licensed wine outlet which does not sell malt beverages; however, under all circumstances wine outlets shall be under the same standards and restrictions as are applicable to malt beverage outlets under this chapter.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-54)
187:
(a) In addition to the annual retail wine license fee required, there is hereby levied an excise tax computed as prescribed by Georgia laws.
(b) The tax shall be paid to the city clerk, by each wholesale distributor, on all wine sold to the retailers in the city, no later than the tenth day of each month based upon the units of wine sold during the previous calendar month by said wholesalers to retailers in the city.
(c) Each wholesale distributor shall furnish to the city clerk a summary of all purchase invoices for wine sold to each retailer in the city on or before the tenth day of each month following such purchases. Said invoices shall show the amount of excise tax paid.
(d) The city shall have the right to audit, and to require production of records from each wholesaler, supplying retailers in the city and from each retailer so applied.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-55)
190:
Retail package dealers shall not: (i) engage in the sale of malt beverages or wine except between the hours of 7:00 a.m. through 1:00 a.m. the following day on Mondays through Fridays; and 7:00 a.m. through 12:00 a.m. on Saturdays; and 12:30 p.m. through 11:30 p.m. on Sundays; or (ii) engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits except between the hours of 9:00 a.m. through 11:45 p.m. Mondays through Saturdays; and 12:30 p.m. through 11:30 p.m. on Sundays; however, retail package dealers shall not permit their outlets to sell malt beverages, wine or distilled spirits on Christmas Day or any other day on which they are required to be closed by the laws of this state. The sale of permitted alcoholic beverages on any local, state, and federal election day is permitted.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-61; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005; Ord. No. 2024-32, 10-28-2024)
191:
(a) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling malt beverages at wholesale within the area of the city shall be $100.00.
(b) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling wine at wholesale within the area of the city shall be $100.00.
(c) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling distilled spirits at wholesale within the area of the city shall be $100.00.
(d) The annual license fee for the privilege of engaging in the business of selling malt beverages and/or wine at retail within the area of the city shall be $500.00.
(e) No license shall be issued for less than the calendar year as herein provided, and in case of revocation or surrender of any license before the expiration of such calendar year, the holder thereof shall not be entitled to receive any refund whatsoever.
(f) The aforesaid license fees herein set shall not be pro-rated for any portion of a year and shall remain the full amount when said calendar year expires with regard to the time the application is made.
(g) The mayor and council of the city shall have the authority to set the annual license fees contained in this section by resolution.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-62; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005)
192:
No license shall be granted to a retailer under any provision or section of this chapter unless the front entrance to the outlet is clearly visible from a public street, road or highway, and the front of said outlet shall have a minimum window at least three feet by four feet, and no screen, blind, curtain, partition, article or things which shall prevent a clear view into the interior of the outlet shall be permitted in the window or upon the doors of any retail outlet. Each retail outlet shall be so lighted that the interior of the store or premises is visible day or night and all parking areas adjacent to or used in connection with said business shall be fully lighted and unobstructed.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-63)
193:
The retail license authorized hereunder are for retail sales in package only and there shall be no consumption on the premises of any outlet of any malt beverages or wine, except those outlets provided for in section 6-62(d).
(1986 Code, § 9-3-64)
194:
No malt beverage nor wine shall be sold to any intoxicated person, nor shall any intoxicated person be allowed to remain upon the premises of any outlet.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-65)
195:
No malt beverages nor wine shall be sold to a minor under any conditions whatsoever. A minor for the purposes of this chapter shall be considered to be any person under 21 years of age. Unless the officer has reasonable cause to believe such person is intoxicated, a law enforcement officer may arrest a person under 21 years of age who purchases or knowingly possesses alcoholic beverages by issuing a citation which shall enumerate the specific charges against the person and either the date upon which the person is to appear to answer the charges or notation that the person will be later notified of the date upon which the person is to appear and answer the charges. The law enforcement officer arresting a person by the issuance of a citation may require such person to deposit a driver's license with the arresting officer to assure the appearance of such person to answer the charges against him. (reference, sections 5A-9901.1(d) and (c) of state alcoholic beverage code).
(1986 Code, § 9-3-66)
196:
No employees of any outlet shall work in said outlet while intoxicated and no employee shall drink any malt beverages, wine, or alcoholic beverages whatsoever while working and employed in any outlet.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-67)
197:
Minors shall not be allowed to congregate or loiter on the premises of any retail store outlet selling malt beverages or wine.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-68)
198:
The commission shall have authority to establish uniform rules and regulations regarding advertising. All advertising must be approved by the commission prior to use. No other signs which will be visible from the exterior of the building shall be permitted.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-69)
199:
All licenses required under this chapter must be posted in a conspicuous place within the outlet, and if said license is not so posted the outlet shall not be authorized to continue in business until the same shall be so posted.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-70)
200:
At all times the retail licensee under this chapter must post within the place of business a copy of this ordinance in a conspicuous place within the outlet.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-71)
201:
All retail licensee's under this chapter are hereby required to comply with all rules and regulations and requirements of the county board of health, state board of health and any and all other state, federal and local authorized public health authorities.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-72)
202:
Retail licenses under this article shall be of three categories as follows:
(1) Retail store licenses. A retail store license as defined herein shall be one issued to a business whose primary function is the sale of food, medicines and related merchandise and the sale of malt/wine beverages at retail is incidental to the operation thereof. All malt/wine beverages must be located within the interior of any such outlet, shall be sacked in containers at the check-out counter of such outlet at time of sale, and no such beverages shall be opened or consumed, either inside or outside the premises.
(2) Private clubs which are affiliated with a nationally chartered organization, either service, athletic or charitable, with a minimum of 200 members, occupying no less than 5,000 square feet, and provided further that the sale of malt beverage or wine shall not be the major part of said business, but only incidental with it's operation.
(3) Other retail commercial buildings which meet the specifications and rules of the commission.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-73)
203:
All license fees required under this chapter shall be paid prior to the issuance of any license.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-74)
204:
For the purpose of this chapter wine which is authorized hereunder is that wine which is authorized to be legally sold and distributed in counties which have not authorized the legal sale of distilled spirits and spirituous liquors as defined by the laws of the state.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-75)
205:
It shall be unlawful for any person, firm or corporation to sell or possess for the purpose of sale or resale of any malt/wine beverages where such does not have a license from the city to sell or possess for sale or resale such beverages. It shall be presumed, as a matter of law, that any person having located on his premises more than 1,440 fluid ounces of malt beverage or five gallons of wine shall have the same in his possession for the purpose of resale.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-76)
206:
Malt beverages and/or wine shall be received at or delivered to the premises of the retail licensee by no other means than by a conveyance owned and operated by a wholesale dealer with a permit from the city to make deliveries in said transportation of malt/wine beverages by any other means shall be grounds for a revocation of a wholesale permit or license. Receipt of malt/wine beverages by any other means by a retail licensee shall be grounds for revocation of a retail license.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-77)
207:
No licenses granted under this chapter shall be transferable from one person to another, nor shall the same be transferable from one outlet (location) to another.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-78)
208:
If the person to whom any license under this chapter is issued does not personally manage the outlet, the name of the manager of the outlet must always be registered with the commission, and the manager of the outlet must meet all the requirements of a person to whom a license could be granted hereunder. If such licensed outlet is not managed directly by the holder of the license, or there is no manager registered as provided thereunder who meets all the requirements hereunder, then said license may be suspended or revoked. If such a manager is changed, the holder of the license must notify the city clerk no later than ten days from the date of the change of such manager and all information required hereunder with regard to managers shall also be furnished to said clerk at said time.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-79; Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
211:
The council shall appoint a five-member "malt and wine beverage control commission," independent of the commission, each member of which shall serve until replaced by a majority vote of the council. The council, by majority vote, shall designate one of the five members of the malt and wine beverage control commission as the "presiding officer." The presiding officer shall moderate all meetings of the malt and wine beverage control commission during his term of office, but shall have no executive functions or powers greater than the other members of the malt and wine beverage control commission. The presiding officer may be removed at any time by majority vote of the city council. A quorum of three members of the commission shall be necessary for the transaction of any business.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-91; Ord. No. 95-03, § 1.5, 3-27-1995)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 95-03, § 1.5, adopted March 27, 1995, changed the title of § 6-91 from "Established; composition" to "Establishment of malt beverage and wine commission."
212:
The alcoholic beverage commission shall have all the powers, duties and responsibilities as are granted to them by the terms and provisions of this entire chapter including but not limited to all other provisions of state law as may be applicable to the sale of alcoholic beverages. It is the intent of this chapter that all of the duties, responsibilities, and decisions pertaining to the granting of licenses, revoking the same, suspending same, and the like, and all other matters pertaining to the control of alcoholic beverages as provided under this chapter shall be vested in said commission as herein provided.
The alcoholic beverage commission shall furnish a copy of the issuance of any license, license renewal, suspension, revocation, appeals, minutes of alcoholic beverage commission meetings and such other documents as the alcoholic beverage commission may designate to the mayor and council, city clerk, city manager, city attorney, chief of police and code of enforcement department. It shall be the responsibility of the city manager to ensure the timely distribution of all documents and information herein above set forth.
The city manager shall upon the filing of any appeal, suspension or revocation of an alcoholic beverage license or any decision concerning same, document the date and time of the filing thereof and shall furnish a copy of same instanter to the alcoholic beverage commission, city attorney, chief of police and code enforcement department.
(1986 Code, § 9-3-92; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005; Ord. No. 2006-23, 11-27-2006)
216:
Licenses for the sale of malt beverages, wine and distilled spirits for on-premises consumption shall be a mere grant or privilege during the term of said license, subject to all the terms and conditions imposed by this chapter and division, and any other related laws of the State of Georgia, the Charter, and this Code. A license for on-premises consumption may be issued as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005)
217:
All sections and divisions of chapter 6 are herein made applicable to division 5, to the extent that same are not in conflict with any section in division 5.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002)
218:
An applicant for on-premises consumption shall be required to submit an application as is set forth in this chapter and pursuant to the requirements of O.C.G.A., § 3-3-2. An application for a license may be denied upon the grounds as is set forth in section 6-28.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002)
219:
The State laws and regulations relating to the sale and distribution of alcoholic beverages in Georgia, as revised and proclamated by the general assembly of the state and by the state revenue department, and especially as they relate to wholesale, retail package sales, and retail sales for consumption on the premises, are hereby incorporated into and made a part of this chapter as if fully set out herein.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002)
220:
Applicants possessing all of the necessary qualifications for the issuance of a license for the sale of malt beverages, wine and/or distilled spirits for consumption on the premises shall be required to possess a city business license and the appropriate state, county, and municipal health department certificates for the sale and service of food and beverages to the general public with a seating capacity of not less than 125 people. It shall be further required of applicants as a condition to the issuance of a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, that said sale of alcoholic beverages shall be ancillary to the primary business of the serving of food which shall consist of at least 80 percent of the gross receipts of the business. A condition of the issuance of a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises is that the food sales of the licensee shall account for the majority of the gross revenue of said business. The licensee shall be required at all reasonable times and places as designated by the city manager and/or the alcoholic beverage commission, to produce financial records and documentation as may be required by the city manager and or the alcoholic beverage commission. The requirements contained herein shall not apply to a wine or growler sample license contained in section 6-134.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005; Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
221:
Licensees for the sale of malt beverages and/or wine for consumption on the premises shall be authorized to sale same as is authorized and permitted in section 6-61.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002)
222:
A license shall be issued for not less than a calendar year, unless hereinafter provided.
(a) The annual license fee for the privilege of selling malt beverages for consumption on premises shall be $500.00.
(b) The annual license fee for the privilege of selling wine for consumption on premises shall be $500.00.
(c) The annual license fee for the privilege of selling distilled spirits for consumption on-premises shall be $2,000.00 for the year 2005, and $4,000.00 commencing January 1, 2006.
(d) Special event license fee for the privilege of selling alcoholic beverages for consumption at event shall be $350.00.
(e) The mayor and council shall be authorized to set the schedule of license fees contained in this section and section 6-128 by resolution.
(f) Sample license fee shall be $200.00.
(Ord. No. 2002-03, 3-25-2002; Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005; Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
223:
In addition to the annual license fees required, there is hereby levied and imposed an excise tax in accordance with the O.C.G.A. § 3-4-130, that shall be paid to the city in the amount of three percent of the charge to the public for the beverages.
(Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005)
224:
Notwithstanding any provisions to the contrary, the alcoholic beverage commission shall have authority to issue a special event license for the sale of alcoholic beverages. Conditioned upon such terms and provisions as may be set forth upon the issuance of said special event permit, provided however, that said issuance does not conflict with state laws.
(Ord. No. 2005-06, 4-11-2005; Ord. No. 2007-13, 5-14-07)
225:
Special event shall mean any organized activity sponsored by a business, organization, corporation, association or individual having as its purpose entertainment, recreation, and or education, such as a festival or celebration, foot or vehicle race, parade or march, rally or assembly which takes place on a public street, sidewalk or right-of-way, or occurs on private property and impacts government services on public right-of-ways or streets. Special events shall not include an occasional family celebration, parties, wedding anniversary and private gatherings.
(Ord. No. 2007-13, 5-14-07)
226:
The applicant for any special event license shall be responsible for the provision of police and sanitation services within the boundaries of the event and for the grant of the license privilege the director of public utilities, director of public works, the chief of police, the fire chief and the code enforcement officer shall approve the impacted government services. In addition each department of the government reviewing an application may recommend in writing certain recommendations or restrictions as deemed necessary to facilitate the event, to comply with other laws or regulations and or to insure the safety, health and welfare of the community. Applicants shall further be responsible for compliance with all laws including but not limited to underage consumption.
(Ord. No. 2007-13, 5-14-07)
227:
As a condition of issuance, the approved applicant agrees to indemnify, hold harmless, release and defined the city, city officials, and officers and employees from and against any and all liability, loss, suits, claims, damages, cost, judgments and expenses including attorney's fees and cost of litigation which in whole or in part result from, or arise out of, or are claim to result from or to arise out of any acts, negligence, errors, or omissions of applicant, applicant's employees, representatives, contractors, subcontractors, agents whatsoever and without limitations.
(Ord. No. 2007-13, 5-14-07)
228:
The safety, health, welfare and good order of all citizens and the community shall be first and foremost and every special event shall be conducted in such a manner as to comport with this standard. The chief of police or fire chief or their representative or their respective designee, may terminate any activity, whether a part of or the entire event, which does not meet the community standard. Upon notification to the applicant to cease any activity, the activity so ordered to be ceased shall immediately be terminated and the continuous of said unauthorized activity shall be unlawful and the applicant could be subject thereto criminal and civil sanctions.
(Ord. No. 2007-13, 5-14-07)
229:
(a) A licensee for the sale of package malt beverages may be issued a license to give or sell samples of tap beer brews for growler's or wine to go in sealed containers (subsection 6-127(f)).
(b) A growler or wine sample shall not exceed one ounce nor shall an individual be offered more than three samples within a 24-hour period.
(c) The intent of the sample license is to permit the customers to lawfully taste a sample of the tap brew or wine so as to make a selection of the brew or wine to be sold for carryout in a sealed container.
(Ord. No. 2011-23, 1-9-2012)
231:
All definitions set forth in the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code (O.C.G.A. Title 3) and State of Georgia regulations, as amended are hereby adopted by this division. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this division, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Applicant means the person, persons, or entity who files forms designated by the city requesting to be issued a privilege license to sell packaged distilled spirits by either wholesale or retail within the city.
Application means the forms an applicant is required to file in order apply to obtain a license to sell packaged distilled spirits in the city.
Bottle means any container, vessel, bottle, or other receptacle used for holding alcoholic beverages. "Unsealed bottle" means any bottle with the original seal cork, cap, or other enclosing device that is either broken, removed, or which the federal revenue strip stamp has been broken.
Church means a permanent building located in an area designated for such use by the zoning ordinances where persons regularly assemble for religious worship, that is publicly designated as a church, but does not include residences or place of businesses also used for religious purposes.
City means the City of Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia.
Construction shall not only mean the process of building a physical structure but shall also include the process of development of plans, designs, obtaining permits, or other approvals necessary to begin erection of a physical structure.
Enforcement officer means a certified City of Fort Oglethorpe Police Officer or other individual who, through specialized knowledge and training, is employed by the city to regulate and enforce compliance with city ordinances.
Distance means the distance established by the most direct route of travel on the ground.
Family member means any person related within the first degree of consanguinity or affinity to the licensee or applicant for a package distilled spirits license.
Federal statutes mean the statutes of the United States now in effect or as may hereinafter be modified.
License means the authorization by the mayor and council to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the city.
Licensee means a person, real or artificial, authorized by the mayor and council to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the city.
Person means any private individual, partnership, joint venture, corporation, limited liability company or any other business entity or association.
Person underage means an individual under the age of 21 years.
Packaged distilled spirits means any alcoholic beverage with an alcohol volume greater than 24 percent sold or transferred at wholesale or retail in any container, vessel, bottle, or other receptacle used for holding alcoholic beverages.
Packaged distilled spirits retailer means a person licensed by the mayor and council to sell packaged distilled spirits in unbroken packages for consumption off-premises.
Premises means the property owned, leased, or controlled by the licensee, including, but not limited to, the building and the parking areas surrounding it, where packaged distilled spirits are sold.
Quality cigars means the sale of handmade cigars rated 85 or above by Cigar Aficionado in the sizes of Petite Corona, Corona, Robusto, Toro, guordo, Panatela, Lonsdale, Churchill, Lancero, Double Corona and Grand Corona.
Retail sale means selling or offering for sale packaged distilled spirits to any member of the public.
School means only such state, county, city, church, or other schools that teach the subjects commonly taught in the common schools and colleges of this state.
State statutes, rules and regulations means all applicable statutes, rules, and regulations of the State of Georgia applicable to the sale of packaged distilled spirits as may now be in effect or which may be amended hereinafter.
Wholesale means the sale of packaged distilled spirits to any person for the purpose of resale.
Words importing the masculine gender shall include the feminine and neuter, and the singular shall include the plural.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022; Ord. No. 2023-26, 9-11-2023)
232:
Every person desiring to obtain a license for the retail or wholesale sale of packaged distilled spirits in the city shall be required under this division to make formal written application to the mayor and council for such privilege, which shall be signed by the applicant and/or agent, if applicable, upon forms to be prepared and provided by the city. All such applicants and agents shall furnish all reasonable data, information and records requested of them by the city. Failure to furnish such data, information, and records within 30 days from the date of a written request from the city for such information shall automatically serve to dismiss the application. Applicants, or those having an interest in the application, by filing an application, agree to produce any such data, information, and records for review by enforcement officers and the mayor and council. Applicants, or those having an interest in the application, by filing an application, agree to submit to an oral interrogation by enforcement officers or by the mayor and council if considered as being important in the ascertainment of the facts relative to an application. The failure to produce such applicant or person of interest within 30 days after being requested in writing to do so shall result in the automatic dismissal of the application. The application must identify the name of the person conducting the business at the premises address contained in the application.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
233:
Any material omission or untrue or misleading information contained in or left out of an original or renewal application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits in the city shall be cause for the denial thereof. If any license has previously been granted based on such misleading statements or material omissions, such shall constitute cause for the revocation of the license.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
234:
Upon filing an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the city with the city clerk, the city shall require the applicant to pay a non-refundable fee to cover the cost of processing the application in the amount of $100.00. Said fee may be amended by resolution of the mayor and council as shall be set from time to time. No application shall be processed without payment of fee.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
235:
The city shall cause an inquiry to be made into the city tax records to determine if an applicant for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the city, or other party with an interest in the application, has any outstanding taxes or special assessments that are delinquent against his property or any other monies owing to the city. No license shall be issued or renewed until such debts are paid in full.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
236:
Upon an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the city being granted by the mayor and council, a license shall be issued to the applicant as of the date the applicant commences his alcoholic beverage business and upon the payment by the applicant of the license fee.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
237:
The denial of an application for a license to sell packaged distilled spirits at wholesale or retail in the city shall be in writing, with the reasons therefore stated, and it shall be mailed or delivered to the applicant at the address of the applicant contained on the application by first class mail. Any applicant aggrieved by the decision of the mayor and council regarding the denial of a license shall be afforded a hearing with an opportunity to present evidence and cross examine opposing witnesses as provided herein.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
238:
When any application for a retail or wholesale package distilled spirits license is denied for cause, or any license is revoked for cause by the mayor and council, the city clerk shall not accept or consider any application by such applicant for a license to operate the same type of business for a period of 24 months from the date of a license denial and 60 months from the date of a revocation of license in the event of a revocation for cause.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
239:
(a) An application for a retail package distilled spirits license may be approved by the mayor and council prior to the applicant obtaining an occupancy permit for a premises if the premises is currently, or will be, under construction.
(b) If the applicant fails to obtain an occupancy permit for the premises so constructed within 12 months of the date of approval of the application to sell packaged distilled spirits at retail in the city, the mayor and council shall conduct a hearing on the record upon the issue of whether to revoke the application for failure to make significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for the premises. Applications previously approved by the mayor and council on July 11, 2022, shall be required to show cause at a hearing before the mayor and council why their applications should not be revoked for failure to make significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for the premises, before revoking those applications (amendment August 28, 2023).
(c) Upon a finding by the mayor and council that sufficient evidence exists to support the revocation of the application for failure to make significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for the premises, the mayor and council may revoke the application. The mayor and council shall notify the applicant of its decision as to applicant's failure to make significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for said premises at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing. Failure of the mayor and council to notify the licensee of its determination at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing shall result in a dismissal of the revocation of the application.
(d) Upon a finding by the mayor and council that sufficient evidence exists that the applicant has made significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for the premises to be used for the retail sales of packaged distilled spirits, the mayor and council may establish a date certain that applicant must obtain said certificate of occupancy for the premises or suffer revocation of the application and/or establish a new hearing date upon the issue of whether to revoke the application for failure to make significant progress toward obtaining a certificate of occupancy for the premises.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022; Ord. No. 2023-26, 9-11-2023)
240:
Except for a license issued to a site under construction, or soon to be under construction, an applicant must open the retail package distilled spirits business in the establishment referred to in the application within six months after its approval by mayor and council. The city clerk shall not issue the license until presented with the applicant's notarized statement stating the applicant is in fact the owner of the business and will open for business on a date certain. The license shall be dated as of the date certain in the affidavit and shall not be effective until that date. Failure to open the licensed establishment within the six-month period or the date stated in the applicant's affidavit shall serve an automatic forfeiture and cancellation of the unused license, and no refund of fees shall be made.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
241:
Any holder of a license issued under this division, who shall begin the operation of the business authorized in the license, but who shall for a period of six consecutive months thereafter cease to operate the business as authorized in the license, shall, upon completion of the six-month period, automatically forfeit his license. Said license shall, by virtue of the failure to operate, be revoked without the necessity of any further action of the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
242:
No person who has any direct financial interest in a license for the sale of package distilled spirits at wholesale shall hold any other license or an interest in any license under the terms of this division.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
243:
It shall be lawful for a licensee to sell packaged distilled spirits at retail at a designated premises location in the city provided that such sales are made in strict compliance with all federal statutes, all state laws, rules and regulations, and all provisions of this division, and provided that such licensee has a valid and duly issued privilege license from the city permitting him or her to sell same. Transfer of ownership or possession of any retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license is prohibited, void and invalid.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
244:
Each licensee shall be responsible for all acts of such licensee as well as the acts of the licensee's officers, employees, agents, and representatives. Any violation of this division by any officer, employee, agent, or representative of a licensee shall constitute a violation of this division by such licensee.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
245:
Citizenship, age, and residency requirements for an applicant for a license to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be as follows:
(1) If the applicant is a person, the person shall be a United States citizen, or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residency, a resident of the city, and at least 21 years of age; provided, however, the person applicant need not be a city resident if the person designates a resident of the city who is at least 21 years of age as his or her agent who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.
(2) If the applicant is a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity, this section shall apply to all its partners, officers, managers, and principal owners. If a corporation or limited liability company, the license shall be issued to the corporation or limited liability company. Where the principal owner or member is not a resident of the city, the corporation or limited liability company shall designate an individual as its agent who must be a resident of the city and at least 21 years of age who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license. For a partnership, the license shall be issued to one of the partners. If a partner is not a resident of the city, the partnership must designate a city resident at least 21 years of age as the partnership's agent who shall be responsible for any matter relating to the license.
(3) Any change in any relationship declared in this division must be filed, when said change is made, with the Fort Oglethorpe Police Chief, or his designee, and failure to do so within a period of 30 days after such change is made shall be grounds for revocation of a license granted under this division by the mayor and council.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
246:
No application for any license required under this division shall be granted where the application, investigation or the evidence presented at a hearing before the mayor and council shows any of the following conditions to exist:
(1) The applicant, principal owner, or his agent has a conviction, as defined in section 6-150(5), or does not have sufficient mental capacity to conduct the business for which application is made or who has been dishonorably discharged from the Armed Services of the United States.
(2) The applicant or any agent, stockholder, partner, or member of the applicant has had any license issued by the city previously revoked within 36 months of the date of the application.
(3) The applicant or his agent, as a previous holder of a license to sell any type of alcoholic beverages in any jurisdiction, has violated any law, regulation or ordinance relating to such business within a 36-month period immediately preceding the date of the application. In the event of a renewal application, offences prosecuted and resolved pursuant to this division shall not be considered.
(4) The applicant's proposed business premises is not properly zoned for the license applied for.
(5) Persons with prior felony criminal convictions.
a. The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this section, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this subsection, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
1. "Convictions" include an adjudication of guilt, a plea of guilty, a plea of nolo contendere, a guilty plea under a first offender statute, or the forfeiture of a bond when charged with a felony;
2. "Principal owner" refers to an individual owning, directly or indirectly, a five percent or more interest in a corporation, partnership, limited partnership, limited liability company or other entity.
b. No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be issued to any individual, partnership, limited partnership, corporation or limited liability company where such individual or any individual who is a principal owner of any partnership, limited partnership, corporation, limited liability company or other entity, or who is the agent responsible for matters relating to the license shall have been convicted under any federal, state or local law of any misdemeanor involving sexual misconduct, dishonesty, possession or use of a controlled substance, or possession of drug paraphernalia within ten years prior to the filing of the application for such license; or, convicted under any federal state or local law of any felony within ten years prior to the filing of the application for such license.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
247:
(a) No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided in this section.
(b) If an individual licensee dies, the licensee's estate shall be allowed to continue to sell packaged distilled spirits for a period of 60 days from the date of death, or until expiration of the license, or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur. However, no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed until such time as a personal representative of the estate, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall make application with the city clerk for authorization to continue to sell for such period.
(c) If a licensee or responsible person, other than the owner, severs such licensees association with a licensed establishment, the establishment may continue to sell packaged distilled spirits for a period of 60 days from the date of such severance, provided a new application is filed with the city clerk within ten days of such severance, and indicates that there has been no change in the ownership of the licensed establishment. If approved by the mayor and council, the term of the new license shall be for the remaining term of the original license and the original license shall terminate as of the date of such approval. No additional license fees, other than administrative fee set by the mayor and council by resolution from time to time, shall be required from the applicant.
(d) Nothing in this section, however, shall prohibit one or more of the partners in a partnership holding a license to withdraw from the partnership in favor of one or more of the partners who were partners at the time of the issuance of the license and who meet the qualifications of a licensee under this article. This subsection shall not prohibit the transfer of stock between persons who held stock in the corporation at the time of issuance of the license, nor shall it prohibit transfers of stock which do not result in any person increasing such person's holdings by a total of ten percent or more of any class stock.
(e) Except as provided in this section, any change in the ownership of any entity granted a license shall cancel and revoke any license issued automatically, without the necessity of any hearing.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
248:
(a) Any licensee authorized to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits at specifically described premises shall be required to surrender the license held without demand, except as otherwise provided in this division, upon any of the following events: Any sale or transfer of an interest in the business of the licensee, whether by an actual sale of any of the licensee's stock or proprietorship or partnership interest to any unregistered person not identified in the licensee's application or upon a sale of all or substantially all of the licensee's assets to any unregistered person. For purposes of this subsection, the term "unregistered person" shall mean any individual, corporation, partnership, limited partnership, club, or association, not shown upon any current application for the specific premises involved. For purposes of this subsection, a sale of all or substantially all the licensee's assets shall include or be deemed to include any bulk sale of inventory or assets at any specifically described premises for which the license holder is licensed to engage in the sale of packaged distilled spirits in the city. For purposes of this subsection, any corporation or limited partnership or association whose stock is traded on any stock exchange recognized by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission shall be excepted from this requirement to the extent of any transfer of shareholding or partnership interests not exceeding five percent in any one trade or transaction.
(b) Time limit. Surrender as provided in this chapter shall be made to the city clerk within 30 days of any event requiring surrender of the license.
(c) Fines for failure to surrender. For failure to surrender the license within the period provided in subsection (b) of this section, the applicant shall be fined an amount as follows:
(1) The sum of $50.00 for failure to surrender within 30 days of the date that any surrender of the alcoholic beverage license is required: and
(2) An additional sum of $10.00 per day for each day thereafter from which the licensee fails or defaults in the surrender of the license after the date upon which the surrender is required.
(d) The city clerk shall assess any penalty against any licensee for failure to surrender the license as required by this section. Notice of assessment shall be by certified letter to the licensee based upon information and belief of the city clerk stating the date that any required surrender should have been made by the licensee. The licensee shall have a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the certified letter from the city clerk of the notice of assessment of the penalty to protest the assessment to the city clerk by presenting evidence or information in writing to the city clerk as to the licensee's position. If the city clerk shall not agree with the licensee's position, the licensee shall have ten days from the date of the written notice of the city clerk's written decision disagreeing with the licensee's protest to request in writing a hearing before the mayor and council. The city clerk shall forward the protest to the mayor and council who shall at its next regular meeting accept, reject, or modify the assessment of the penalty.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
249:
A license issued under this article shall expire automatically and without notice upon the occurrence of a delinquency of 20 days in:
(1) Filing any required monthly report under this chapter; or
(2) Paying over any required excise tax levied under this chapter or any other indebtedness owed to the city.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
250:
Whenever the state department of revenue shall revoke any permit or license to sell at wholesale or retail any packaged distilled spirits, any license issued under this division for the same licensed premises shall thereupon be automatically revoked without any action by the mayor and council, or any city officer, and the licensee shall not be entitled to any refund of any license fee theretofore paid to the city.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
251:
The mayor and the chief of police are each delegated the authority to suspend any license issued under this division for due cause in any emergency situation, and the suspension shall be made effective immediately and shall remain in force until a hearing before the mayor and council is held pursuant to section 6-157, section 6-158, and section 6-159.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
252:
When the mayor or chief of police find a violation of any section of this division for which the licensee shall have his packaged distilled spirits license suspended or revoked, all alcoholic beverage licenses of the licensee under this article shall be so suspended or revoked.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
253:
(a) Due cause hearing; defined; cost of hearing.
(1) No license which has been issued or which may be issued pursuant to this article shall be suspended or revoked, except as provided in section 6-155, except for due cause and after a hearing as provided in this division.
(b) The term "due cause" for the purposes of this chapter of the Code shall include, but not be limited to:
(1) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty, plea of first offender, or plea of nolo contendere by the licensee or any person holding an interest in the license for any felony, any law, administrative regulation, or ordinance involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or narcotics, or tax laws.
(2) Conviction of, or the entering of a plea of guilty, plea of first offender, or plea of nolo contendere by the licensee or any person holding an interest in the license for any sex offense, or when the licensee permits on-premises consumption.
(3) Material falsification of any fact given in an application for a license issued under this division or bearing upon the licensee's qualification therefore. Any act, which may be construed as a subterfuge to circumvent any of the qualifications for a license under this division.
(4) Violation of any provision of this division, or any failure to meet or maintain any standard or regulation prescribed by this division as a condition or qualification for holding a license.
(5) Any other factor known to or discovered by the city whereby it is objectively shown the licensee, any of the licensee's employees or any person holding an interest in a license, has engaged in conduct at or involving the licensed business or has permitted conduct on the licensed premises that constitutes a violation of federal or state law, local ordinance or administrative regulations involving alcoholic beverages, gambling, narcotics or sex offenses. Same shall create a rebuttable presumption that the violative act was done with the knowledge or consent of the licensee.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
254:
The city clerk shall notify the licensee of any charge of conduct or offense subject to penalty, suspension or revocation or any combination thereof. If the potential sanction is suspension or revocation the notice shall also state the place and time the mayor and council will hear the charges against the licensee. The notice may also contain such additional information as the city clerk may deem appropriate. The notice shall be delivered to the licensee at least five days prior to the hearing date, by personal delivery, or by first class mail addressed to the licensee at the address contained in licensee's application, or by posting the notice on the front door of the licensed premises. In the case of delivery by first class mail the notice shall be deemed delivered two days after being deposited into the U.S. mail properly addressed and with adequate postage.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
255:
(a) The mayor and council shall conduct a hearing on the record on any revocation or suspension of a packaged distilled spirits license. The licensee shall be allowed to appear at said hearing and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses. The mayor and council shall notify the licensee of its decision as to revocation or suspension of the license at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing. Upon a finding by the mayor and council that sufficient evidence exists to support the revocation or suspension, the mayor and council may revoke or suspend the license of the licensee for up to a period not to exceed 60 months. Failure of the mayor and council to notify the licensee of its determination at such hearing or in writing no later than 30 days after such hearing shall result in a dismissal of the charge.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
256:
When an alcoholic beverage license is revoked, suspended or expires, the city shall not be required to refund any portion of the license fee.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
257:
When any license for selling packaged distilled spirits is revoked, suspended, or automatically expires, all signs indicating that such packaged distilled spirits may be sold or purchased at that premises shall be removed from the premises, both outside and inside.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
258:
(1) The number of packaged distilled spirits licenses for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits at designated locations in the city, issued under this division and outstanding within the City of Fort Oglethorpe, shall be limited to three licenses, with one such license issued for district A, one such license issued for district B, and one such license issued for district C.
(2) With respect to the issuance of the first three retail sale of distilled spirits licenses, if more than one properly completed application is submitted to the city for a respective district and approved by the mayor and council at the time of the publicly announced deadline for applications has expired, the city will then have a lottery drawing for each respective district where more than one properly completed application is approved by the mayor and council. An applicant may submit an application for more than one district, but in the event the applicant's application is drawn in the lottery, all other applications of that applicant shall become null and void. In the event a district does not receive an application by the deadline mentioned above, the city will then accept additional properly completed applications for an additional 30 days in that respective district with a lottery to follow if there are more than one properly completed applications approved by the mayor and council for that district. If no applications are received during the second period for that district the license will then be awarded to the first qualified applicant. In the event of a surrender, suspension for more than 180 days, or the revocation of a retail distilled spirits license, the city will hold a lottery drawing for the vacant license with such lottery being held not less than 60 days from the effective date of such suspension, surrender, termination or revocation. With respect to such lottery, the city shall issue public notice for the submission of applications not less than 30 days prior to the date of the lottery drawing. For purposes of this section, the effective date shall be the date upon which all appeals, if any, are no longer available to a licensee or have otherwise been exhausted.
(3) Any lottery conducted under this division, if more than one district is being licensed, shall be conducted in the following order: District A, then district B, then district C.
(4) If an applicant that is selected by lottery fails to complete the process required by the city to obtain a license to sell packaged distilled spirits within the time limits set forth in this division, then the city will select by lottery another applicant from the previous pool of properly submitted applications.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
259:
(a) There is hereby created within the city three districts in which only one retail sale of packaged distilled spirits license may be issued per district.
(1) District A shall be designated as containing those eligible properties that have road frontage access directly along Battlefield Parkway from Fort Town Drive to the City limits at Pine Grove Road.
(2) District B shall be designated as containing those eligible properties that have road frontage access directly from Highway 41 at the state line to Cloud Springs Road and road frontage access along Cloud Springs Road to Roadway Drive.
(3) District C shall be designated as containing those eligible properties that have road frontage access directly from Highway 27 at Cloud Springs Road to Gilbert Drive and road frontage access from Highway 27 along Battlefield Parkway to Fant Drive.
(4) A map depicting said districts shall be maintained in the city clerk's office at city hall.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
260:
(a) No retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license shall be issued until it has been approved by the mayor and council.
(b) No retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits license shall be approved unless all sections of this division, state laws, rules and regulations have been met by the applicant.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
261:
Every license issued under this article shall be a mere grant or privilege to carry on such business during the term of the license, subject to all the terms and conditions imposed by this division and related laws, applicable sections of state law, rules and regulations and other city ordinances and resolutions relating to such business.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
262:
A packaged distilled spirits licensee may hold more than one type of retail license, including but not limited to wine, malt beverage and pouring license, provided that each license must be approved by the mayor and council. Licensees seeking more than one licenses for an individual premise must meet the requirements of each license.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
263:
It shall be unlawful for a licensee to engage in any activity pertaining to the sale of alcoholic beverages except as authorized by the type of license held.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
264:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person operating a premise licensed for the retail sale of wine and malt beverages to store or have on the premises any packaged distilled spirits for retail sales without a license therefore.
(b) Holders of a pouring distilled spirits license shall not be permitted to sell packaged distilled spirits.
(c) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to sell packaged distilled spirits for home delivery.
(d) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to sell packaged distilled spirits through a drive through window, door, or other convenience.
(e) Packaged distilled spirits licensees shall not be permitted to operate, store, or maintain power coin operated amusements machines in the business premises licensed to sell by retail packaged distilled spirits. No form of entertainment, including pinball machines, lottery, bingo, music machines or similar devices, shall be permitted in any premises used for packaged retail distilled spirits sales. No seating facilities, other than for employees, shall be permitted.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
265:
Each licensee for the sale of packaged distilled spirits shall have his license posted conspicuously in the place of business. The failure of a licensee to display the license conspicuously in his place of business shall be a violation of this division.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
266:
(a) A license issued for the retail package sales of distilled spirits shall be valid only for the operation of said purpose upon the property proposed in the licensee's application and any change of location shall be cause for revocation of the license.
(b) No retail package distilled spirits license shall be issued for the operation of same where such would be a prohibited use under the city's zoning ordinance in effect at time of issuance.
(c) No license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits at retail shall be issued for a location where the proposed place of business is located on property the owner of which has any direct or indirect interest or association, including ownership, financial or governing, in any other property within the City of Fort Oglethorpe that operates another retail or wholesale packaged distilled spirits business. For purposes of this section, "owner" shall mean and include an individual, partner, corporation, company, association, or other business entity.
(d) To assure that these requirements are satisfied, no original or renewal license shall be issued for any location until a majority of the members of the city council have approved the proposed location as being suitable for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits after a consideration of this matter at a properly advertised public meeting of the city council.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
267:
(a) The physical locations designated by an applicant for use in the sale by retail of packaged distilled spirits shall be a newly constructed free-standing building. The front of the building must have a brick, stone, or stucco facade. The remaining exterior elevations must meet applicable City of Fort Oglethorpe UDC requirements. Retail packaged distilled spirits premises shall not be made from or out of a manufactured, movable or any prefabricated type of building.
(b) The minimum square footage of the premises display area within a structure shall be 5,000 square feet. Excess storage, not including display areas, must be no less than 500 square feet within the structure but separate from the retail display floor. No separate modules or buildings are allowed, and no storage is permitted outside.
(c) All premises in the city used for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits shall be located on a ground floor level. Each premises shall have only one main entrance for use by the public as a means of ingress and egress for the purpose of purchasing packaged distilled spirits at retail. Notwithstanding, when a premise is located on the corner of two public streets such premises may maintain a door opening on each of the public streets.
(d) All premises used by a licensee for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits shall have night lights surrounding the premises and shall be equipped with a functioning security system, which includes a burglar alarm system on the inside of the premises and at least one indoor and one outdoor camera with video storage capability. Security bars or other types of window or door obstructions are prohibited.
(e) The windows in such premises of licensee shall not be obstructed or obscured by any object, including, but not limited to signage, shelves, inventory, or displays and shall be arranged so that passersby and law enforcement personnel on the street can view the premises by looking through windows opening onto the streets. This requirement shall apply to all sides of structures facing streets. Proposed plans and drawings must be furnished to the mayor and council as a part of the application. All plans for such premises must receive approval from the mayor and council prior to the commencement of construction.
(f) All premises utilized by a licensee for the purpose of retail packaged distilled spirits sales shall be subject to applicable zoning, building, and city land development regulations.
(g) A license issued under this division for a retail package distilled spirits sales location shall be valid only for the operation of such business upon the property proposed in the application and any change of location shall be cause for revocation of the license.
(h) No license shall be issued for the operation of a retail packaged distilled spirits business where such premises would be a prohibited use under the city's zoning ordinance in effect at time of issuance.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
268:
Sworn officers of the police department and code enforcement officers shall have the authority to inspect establishments licensed under this division during the hours in which the premises are open for business. These inspections shall be made for the purpose of verifying compliance with the requirements of this division and state law. This section is not intended to limit the authority of any other city officer to conduct inspections authorized by other sections of the Fort Oglethorpe Code of Ordinances or state law.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
269:
An annual retail and wholesale packaged distilled spirits license fee shall be paid in advance on or before January 15th of each year, in the sum of $5,000.00. Any new license granted during a calendar year shall not be prorated for the remainder of the calendar year.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
270:
(a) A distilled spirit tasting permit for purposes of this section shall be limited to a person possessing a current license from the city for the retail sale of packaged distilled spirits and a valid current distilled spirits license from the state.
(b) Any tasting occurring on the premises of a business possessing a tasting permit shall be limited to an area that is separated from the retail area of the premises by walls or other partitions that prohibit pedestrian traffic through the tasting area.
(c) An eligible licensee may petition the city for a tasting permit provided the licensee holds a valid license for the sale of packaged distilled spirits issued by the city.
(d) A tasting permit shall allow the licensee to offer or sell samples in connection with an instructional or educational promotion and the samples must be consumed in the presence of a representative of the licensed business.
(e) A tasting permit shall allow the permittee to offer 26 tasting events per year, for no more than one time per day, for a maximum of four hours, and only during the hours the licensed premises may lawfully sell unbroken packages of distilled spirits.
(f) A tasting event may only include one type of distilled spirit per event, may include more than one brand of each type of distilled spirit, and no more than four brands may be open at any one time during the tasting event.
(g) A tasting permit shall be subject to all laws, rules and regulations of the city and state, including O.C.G.A. § 3-3-26 and Rule 560-2-5-05 of the state department of revenue, alcohol, and tobacco division, and shall be subject to suspension or revocation for violation thereof.
(h) Said tasting permit need only be applied for once and may be automatically renew when said packaged distilled spirits license is renewed. Provided, however, that the city may revoke or suspend such tasting permit and/or impose such conditions on its operation at the city's discretion for violation of this division or in furtherance of the health, safety, and welfare of the city's inhabitants.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
271:
Each retail licensee for the sale of distilled spirits shall conspicuously display within the interior of the licensed premises not less than four copies of a printed price list for the packaged distilled spirits offered for sale. However, a licensee, in lieu of having four copies of a printed list, may have the price placed on the bottles or on the bottom of the shelf where beverages are exhibited for sale.
No price or prices for the retail sale of distilled spirits shall be displayed in any show window or any place visible from the outside the premises where retail packaged distilled spirits are sold.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
State Law reference— See O.C.G.A. § 3-4-26.
272:
All wholesalers licensed under this division shall file a certified statement with the city of their gross sales in the city for the preceding calendar month on or before the 20th of the following month.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
273:
Distilled spirits deliveries and sales by wholesalers under this division shall only be made to retailers that are properly licensed for the operation of retail packaged distilled spirits sales in the city. Deliveries shall be made in a conveyance owned and operated by the licensed wholesaler. Deliveries of inventory shall only occur only at the rear of the premises through the designated rear entrance to the premises.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
274:
Retail licensees under this division shall not buy or accept deliveries of packaged distilled spirits from wholesalers not licensed under this division. Retail licensees under this division shall only accept deliveries of packaged distilled spirits to the premises for which the license is issued and by no means other than a conveyance owned and operated by a wholesaler licensed as required by this division. However, by written request to the mayor and council and upon the granting of permission by the mayor and council in writing, deliveries may, in special instances, be made otherwise upon the terms and conditions as prescribed by the mayor and council as to each such delivery.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
275:
It shall be a violation of this division for any person to sell at retail within the city any distilled spirits on which the taxes provided for in this division have not been paid.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
276:
In addition to all other taxes or license fees imposed upon retail dealers engaged in the city in the business of selling distilled spirits, as defined in this chapter, there is imposed and levied upon all such licensees an excise tax, to be computed and collected as set forth in this division.
(Ord. No. 2022-01, 2-8-2022)
